<!-- Source: README.md -->

# @codenhub/skills

A curated set of agent skills and a CLI that installs them into the right folders for your agent tools. Choose the workflows you want, then install them in a project, in your home directory, or both.

## Installation

Run the installer without adding it to a project:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest
```

Or use npm:

```sh
npx @codenhub/skills@latest
```

## Usage

Run the command from your project directory. In an interactive terminal, the wizard asks where to install, whether to include all skills or choose a subset, which agent harnesses to target, and whether to clean their skills folders first. Cleanup is off by default.

For a repeatable install without prompts, select skills and destinations explicitly:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --local --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development --harnesses="Claude Workspace,Codex Workspace"
```

The collection covers planning and implementation (`brainstorming`, `test-driven-development`, `coding`, `ponytail`), review and delivery (`audit`, `babysit-pr`), creative work (`branding`, `design`, `logo-design`, `motion-graphics`, `naming`), and agent guidance and writing. See the [skill catalog](docs/skills.md) for every skill and when it applies.

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md): Complete package documentation.
- [Bundled skills](docs/skills.md): Choose skills and understand their format and versioning.
- [CLI installer](docs/cli.md): Options, destinations, and harness behavior.
- [Security and failures](docs/security-and-failures.md): Cleanup risks, partial installs, and recovery.
- [Changelog](docs/changelog/index.md): Release history.

## Requirements

- Node.js 24 or newer.
- Filesystem permission to read source skills and modify selected destinations.
- An interactive terminal (TTY) for the wizard; explicit CLI options support automation.

## Notes

- Existing files are merged and overwritten by default; stale files are not removed unless `--cleanup` is used.
- `--cleanup` recursively removes each selected harness's entire skills directory before installation.
- Installation writes directly to disk without rollback. Back up customized skills before updating; see [failure behavior](docs/security-and-failures.md).
- The package provides an installer CLI, with no supported programmatic library imports.

## License

Licensed under Apache-2.0. Bundled skills include adapted third-party material; see [NOTICE](NOTICE) and [skill provenance](docs/provenance.md).

<!-- Source: docs/index.md -->

# Install and manage agent skills

Each agent tool expects skills in particular folders. Using several tools can mean copying the same skill directories into each project and into your home directory, then repeating the work when they change. `@codenhub/skills` gives you a curated collection and an installer that puts your choices in those folders. The folder names can remain someone else's hobby.

An agent harness is the application that runs an agent, such as Claude or Codex. A skill gives that agent instructions for a particular kind of work. This collection covers planning, coding, review, design, branding, writing, and maintaining agent guidance. You can install just the skills you need; each is packaged with its supporting files and any required notices.

These docs follow a project using Claude and Codex. We start with `brainstorming` to clarify a change before implementation and `test-driven-development` to implement it with tests, then install the same pair globally for use across projects.

## Quick start

With Node.js 24 or newer, open an interactive terminal in your project directory and run:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest
```

The npm equivalent is `npx @codenhub/skills@latest`. Neither command adds a dependency to your project.

In the wizard, choose local scope, decline the all-skills option, select `brainstorming` and `test-driven-development`, and choose `Claude Workspace` and `Codex Workspace`. Leave cleanup off to keep other installed skills. The installer copies the selected directories into `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` under the current directory.

To make the same selection without prompts:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --local --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development --harnesses="Claude Workspace,Codex Workspace"
```

Any argument except `--include-drafts` switches off the wizard. Without arguments outside an interactive terminal, the installer selects all bundled skills and detected local harnesses. The [CLI guide](docs/cli.md#modes) explains detection and how to choose destinations explicitly.

## Before installing

You need filesystem permission to read the bundled skills and write to every selected destination. Review the skills you install: they contain instructions an agent may follow and may include scripts. The installer copies files; your harness determines how to load and use them. There are no supported programmatic library imports.

Existing files at matching paths are overwritten, directories are merged, and stale files remain. Installation has no rollback. The optional `--cleanup` removes the entire selected skills folder, including skills from other sources. Read [Security and failures](docs/security-and-failures.md) before using cleanup or updating customized installations.

## Reading path

1. [Bundled skills](docs/skills.md): choose workflows, understand what a skill contains, and learn the format, quality rules, and versioning policy.
2. [CLI installer](docs/cli.md): install the pair for Claude and Codex, repeat it globally, and learn all options, destinations, and harness differences.
3. [Security and failures](docs/security-and-failures.md): understand what an update can overwrite, diagnose a partial install, and interpret exit codes.
4. [Skill provenance](docs/provenance.md): check origins, licenses, and the notices to preserve when sharing installed skills.

The [changelog](docs/changelog/index.md) records release changes. The installed `SKILL.md` and its accompanying files describe the workflows for the version you installed.

Start with [Bundled skills](docs/skills.md) to decide which ones belong in your project.

<!-- Source: docs/skills.md -->

# Choose your skills

A skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file: instructions that tell an agent when and how to carry out a particular kind of work. It can also include references, scripts, assets, and harness metadata. Installing a skill puts that folder where your agent tool can find it; the harness decides when to load it, and the agent follows its instructions during the task. A skill supplies a workflow, rather than a guarantee about the result.

For our Claude and Codex project, start with `brainstorming` when a feature needs its requirements clarified, then `test-driven-development` when implementation begins. You do not need the whole collection to use that pair. Each skill stands on its own.

## Bundled catalog

The IDs in the first column are the directory names accepted by `--skills`. Choose by the work you want the agent to do:

| Skill ID                  | When the agent uses it                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brainstorming`           | Before implementation, when requirements or behavior need collaborative design.                                                                      |
| `test-driven-development` | When changing code behavior: write a failing test, implement, then refactor.                                                                         |
| `coding`                  | When writing or changing code, to build it with consistent defaults and handle inputs, failures, state, and sibling paths, with tests written first. |
| `ponytail`                | When coding, to choose the simplest working solution and avoid speculative code.                                                                     |
| `audit`                   | When reviewing code, packages, or pull requests for defects, vulnerabilities, contract problems, or readiness to ship.                               |
| `ponytail-review`         | When reviewing complexity, finding code to simplify or delete, or listing deferred work and shortcuts.                                               |
| `babysit-pr`              | When asked to see a GitHub pull request through CI and review, fixing checks and answering reviewers until it can merge.                             |
| `subagent-specialist`     | When work can be delegated: choose tasks, brief workers, review their results, and integrate them.                                                   |
| `agents-md-improver`      | When writing, auditing, or trimming repository agent instructions, including `AGENTS.md` and files that load it.                                     |
| `project-template`        | When creating a project from the shared project template, comparing an existing project with it, or migrating off its old manifest.                  |
| `writing-skills`          | When authoring, reviewing, or fixing agent skills and evaluating whether their instructions work.                                                    |
| `branding`                | When defining brand strategy, voice, messaging, or a visual identity system and its guidelines.                                                      |
| `naming`                  | When generating, researching, comparing, or choosing names, including names in code.                                                                 |
| `design`                  | When building or reviewing visual interfaces, typography, layout, color, accessibility, or interface motion in any medium.                           |
| `logo-design`             | When creating or refining a logo, mark, favicon, or app icon, through SVG files and usage rules.                                                     |
| `motion-graphics`         | When storyboarding, animating, or rendering a video built with web technology.                                                                       |
| `caveman`                 | When the user asks for shorter answers or a compressed communication mode.                                                                           |
| `caveman-commit`          | When writing a commit message or preparing staged changes for a commit, using the project's convention.                                              |
| `playful-tone`            | When the user asks for or agrees to a lighter, humorous tone in docs or other public text.                                                           |

Planning and coding skills cover the path from a proposed change to implementation. Review and delivery skills help inspect that work and move it through a pull request. Creative skills cover the name, identity, interface, and video around a product. The guidance and writing skills help maintain the instructions and text that surround the work. Pick the parts you use; a full collection is optional.

## Skill format

You only need this section when inspecting a bundle or authoring a skill. The `skills/` tree is shipped product content: its instructions and supporting files are read by agent harnesses, rather than published as package-documentation pages.

Each skill occupies one immediate child directory under a source skills directory and must contain `SKILL.md` with that exact casing:

```text
skills/
  example-skill/
    SKILL.md
    NOTICE
    agents/
    references/
    scripts/
    assets/
```

The installer looks only at immediate child directories and recognizes a skill by the presence of `SKILL.md`. It does not search nested folders for more skills. It copies the whole skill directory subject to its [harness-specific `agents` exclusion](docs/cli.md#harness-behavior).

The supported metadata is a flat frontmatter block at the beginning of `SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: example-skill
description: Use when an agent needs the example workflow.
---
```

The installer reads `name` and `description` for the selection screen. The directory name is the skill ID used in commands and destination paths. A missing or empty `name` falls back to that ID; a missing or empty `description` displays no description. Bundled skills must provide both fields under the quality rules below.

Keep those fields on flat `key: value` lines. The installer reads a frontmatter block at the beginning of the file, allowing a leading byte-order mark, with `---` delimiters starting their own lines. It splits each metadata line at its first colon and trims surrounding whitespace. Values remain strings; lines without a colon are ignored, and a repeated key takes its last value. Without a matching block, the installer reads no metadata and uses the fallbacks.

For a value starting with a single or double quote, the installer takes the text up to the next matching quote and strips the quotes; text after that closing quote is ignored. For an unquoted value, whitespace followed by `#` starts a trailing comment. Quote a description containing a literal ` #` to retain it. This is a limited reader, not a full YAML parser: it does not interpret nested structures, arrays, multiline values, type conversions, or escape sequences. In particular, `description: >` or `description: |` displays the indicator instead of the following paragraph. Put the complete description on one line.

Supporting Markdown, YAML, notices, examples, and reference files may accompany `SKILL.md`. Their meaning is harness- or skill-specific and is not interpreted by the package.

## Quality rules

Bundled skills follow the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) and the authoring guidance in the bundled `writing-skills` skill. The package test suite enforces the rules that can be checked mechanically, so `pnpm test skills` fails when a bundled skill breaks one:

- `name` matches the directory, uses lowercase letters, digits, and single hyphens, is at most 64 characters, and contains neither `anthropic` nor `claude`.
- `description` is a single line of 1 to 1024 characters, without XML tags or a folded or literal multiline indicator. `name` must also contain no XML tags.
- Frontmatter uses only the specification's keys: `name`, `description`, `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, and `allowed-tools`.
- The `SKILL.md` body is under 500 lines.
- A skill holds only `SKILL.md`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSE`, `agents/`, `references/`, `scripts/`, and `assets/`.
- Files that `SKILL.md` references exist inside the skill and use forward slashes, and every file in `references/` is referenced from `SKILL.md`.
- Reference files do not reference other files in the skill, and those over 100 lines open with a `## Contents` section.
- A skill's Markdown files do not name another bundled skill, since the user may not have it installed.
- `agents/openai.yaml` defines `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`.

The rest of the authoring guidance, such as how a description is phrased or whether a change was evaluated, needs judgment and is covered in review. Drafts are checked for valid metadata only.

## Versioning

From 1.0, the version of a release says what changes for someone who has the skills installed:

- **Major:** a skill is removed or renamed. A skill ID is the directory the installer writes, and the installer leaves an old directory in place, so a removed or renamed skill stays installed until someone deletes it.
- **Minor:** a skill is added, or an existing skill's triggers, rules, or workflow change.
- **Patch:** editorial changes to a skill, such as wording, formatting, or links, with no intended change in behavior.

The CLI follows SemVer as usual. Rejected: treating every change to a skill's behavior as breaking. Nearly every skill change alters what an agent does, so that rule would make almost every release a major one, and the version would no longer tell consumers which upgrades need their attention.

Use the installed `SKILL.md` and accompanying assets as the authoritative skill content for the installed package version.

## Drafts

Skills still in development live in `drafts/` in the repository, in the same format. They are not published, not listed here, and not installed unless the CLI is run from a checkout with `--include-drafts` (see the [CLI guide](docs/cli.md#draft-skills)). Promoting a draft means moving its directory to `skills/` and adding it to this inventory and to [Skill provenance](docs/provenance.md).

## Third-party material

Several bundled skills adapt third-party material; the provenance table lists which. Package and per-skill notices travel with the relevant assets. See [Skill provenance](docs/provenance.md) and the package [NOTICE](NOTICE) before redistributing or modifying them.

Next, use the [CLI installer](docs/cli.md) to put your chosen skills in the project folders Claude and Codex read.

<!-- Source: docs/cli.md -->

# Install skills in your agent tools

Once you have [chosen skills](docs/skills.md), the installer copies their folders into the locations your agent tools read. This guide installs `brainstorming` and `test-driven-development` for Claude and Codex in one project, then makes the same pair available globally.

The executable is named `codenhub-skills`. Run it without adding a project dependency through a package executor:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest
```

Use `npx @codenhub/skills@latest` for the npm equivalent. Node.js 24 or newer is required.

## Start in a project

Open a terminal in the repository directory where you want the skills. Local paths are relative to the current directory, so running from a subdirectory installs there; the installer does not search upward for a repository root.

Run the command above in an interactive terminal, then:

1. Choose **Locally (project workspace)**, the default scope.
2. Answer **No** to installing all skills. The default is **Yes**; declining opens the individual selection screen, initially with all skills checked.
3. Keep only `brainstorming` and `test-driven-development` selected.
4. Select `Claude Workspace` and `Codex Workspace`, clearing any other checked harnesses.
5. Leave cleanup at its default, **No**, to retain other installed skills.

Use Up and Down to move, Space to toggle checkboxes, and Enter to confirm a step. Backspace or Left returns to the previous step where offered. Ctrl+C cancels the wizard. Once you confirm the cleanup step, installation starts.

Each skill becomes a child directory under `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`. For example, Codex receives `.agents/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`. Missing destination directories are created. By default, existing directories are merged and matching files are overwritten; files present only at the destination remain. Back up local edits before updating.

The installer copies files and reports the result. Consult your harness's instructions for loading installed skills; the package does not validate that a harness can interpret every bundled file.

## Modes

The wizard appears only when stdin is a TTY (an interactive terminal) and no arguments are supplied, except that `--include-drafts` alone keeps it interactive. Scope, skill selection, harnesses, and cleanup are all choices in the wizard. Detected harness paths are preselected; change that selection before confirming if you want fewer destinations.

When stdin is not a TTY, or any other argument is supplied, the CLI does not prompt. Even `--local` alone starts an install with defaults: all skills, local scope, detected harnesses, and no cleanup. Use explicit selections in scripts so the result does not depend on which folders already exist.

Detection means the destination skills folder or its parent exists; it does not check whether the harness application is installed. For example, an existing `.claude/` directory detects `Claude Workspace` even without `.claude/skills/`. Detection is restricted to the selected scope. If nothing is detected, the command fails. Choose labels with `--harnesses` to create their destinations, or use `--all-harnesses` to opt into every destination in that scope.

## Repeat the selection without prompts

This installs our two skills for Claude and Codex in the current repository, whether or not their folders already exist:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --local --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development --harnesses="Claude Workspace,Codex Workspace"
```

For the same pair under your home directory, change both the scope and the labels:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --global --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development --harnesses="Claude Global,Codex Global"
```

Global scope uses fixed locations under your home directory, regardless of the current project. To do both installs in one run, use `--both` and list all four labels:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --both --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development --harnesses="Claude Workspace,Codex Workspace,Claude Global,Codex Global"
```

Local and global copies are separate files. Updating one does not update the other. If both are installed, your harness determines how it resolves them.

## Options

| Option               | Behavior                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--local`            | Use workspace destinations. This is the default scope.                                |
| `--global`           | Use destinations under the current user's home directory.                             |
| `--both`             | Include both workspace and global destinations.                                       |
| `--skills=<list>`    | Install comma-separated, case-sensitive skill IDs.                                    |
| `--all-skills`       | Install every available skill. This is the default; drafts are included when enabled. |
| `--harnesses=<list>` | Install to comma-separated harness labels, matched case-insensitively.                |
| `--all-harnesses`    | Select every harness valid for the chosen scope.                                      |
| `--cleanup`          | Remove entire selected skills destination roots before copying. Off by default.       |
| `--include-drafts`   | Also offer draft skills. Works only from a repository checkout.                       |
| `--help`, `-h`       | Print command help.                                                                   |

Harness labels include their scope, for example `Claude Workspace` and `Claude Global`. A label supplied to `--harnesses` must be valid for the selected scope. Quote the whole list as shown above to keep labels with spaces in one argument.

Use the `=` form for list options: `--skills=brainstorming`, not `--skills brainstorming`. Lists trim whitespace, ignore empty comma-separated items, and remove repeated identical entries, but must contain at least one item. Unknown skill IDs and invalid harness labels fail before installation.

Prefer one scope option and one selection form per list. If repeated, the last scope option wins, and the last `--skills` or `--harnesses` list replaces earlier lists. `--all-skills` and `--all-harnesses` take precedence over their respective lists, though a syntactically empty list still fails. Unknown arguments fail. The skill sources load first, so a loading failure still exits with status 1, such as `--include-drafts` in the published package, which ships no drafts. After that, `--help` or `-h` takes precedence over every other argument, including unknown or invalid ones: it prints usage and exits with status 0 without installing.

## Install Destinations

Workspace paths resolve from the process's current working directory. Global paths resolve from the current user's home directory. The `Agent Skills` destinations are the cross-harness standard locations (`.agents/skills`) that most harnesses read natively; install there, rather than to a harness's own directory, when the harness reads both.

| Harness      | Workspace destination | Global destination           |
| ------------ | --------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| Agent Skills | `.agents/skills`      | `~/.agents/skills`           |
| Antigravity  | `.agents/skills`      | `~/.gemini/config/skills`    |
| Claude       | `.claude/skills`      | `~/.claude/skills`           |
| Cline        | `.cline/skills`       | `~/.cline/skills`            |
| Codex        | `.agents/skills`      | `~/.agents/skills`           |
| Copilot      | `.github/skills`      | `~/.copilot/skills`          |
| Cursor       | `.cursor/skills`      | `~/.cursor/skills`           |
| Gemini CLI   | `.gemini/skills`      | `~/.gemini/skills`           |
| Kiro         | `.kiro/skills`        | `~/.kiro/skills`             |
| OpenCode     | `.opencode/skills`    | `~/.config/opencode/skills`  |
| Trae         | `.trae/skills`        | `~/.trae/skills`             |
| Windsurf     | `.windsurf/skills`    | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills` |
| ZCode        | `.zcode/skills`       | `~/.zcode/skills`            |

Several labels resolve to the same directory because the harnesses read it too: `Agent Skills Workspace`, `Antigravity Workspace`, and `Codex Workspace` share `.agents/skills`; `Agent Skills Global` and `Codex Global` share `~/.agents/skills`. Selecting labels that share a destination installs each skill once rather than copying it repeatedly.

This means selecting both `Agent Skills Workspace` and `Codex Workspace` does not give you two independent installations. They address the same files, so updates or cleanup affect the skills read by every harness using that path.

## Harness Behavior

Destinations selected through a Codex label receive the complete bundled skill directory, including an `agents` directory when a skill has one. Every other destination excludes entries whose base name is exactly `agents` at any depth. When a Codex label shares a destination with other selected labels, the shared copy keeps the `agents` directory. Other references, examples, notices, and supporting files are copied unchanged.

In our example, Codex gets each skill's `agents/openai.yaml` when present; Claude's copy excludes it. Selecting only `Agent Skills Workspace` also excludes `agents` entries, even though Codex reads that destination. Select a Codex label when you want its metadata included. Exclusion skips source entries; it does not delete an `agents` folder left by an earlier install.

## Destructive Cleanup

`--cleanup` recursively removes each selected harness's entire skills destination before installation. This deletes all content in that directory, including skills and files not managed by `@codenhub/skills`. In our local example, adding it removes both `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` as whole directories, even though only two skills are selected. Labels that share a destination, such as `Codex Workspace` and `Agent Skills Workspace`, remove that one directory once.

All selected roots are cleaned before any skill is copied. Back up those directories and check the current working directory and selected scope first. To remove a single stale skill, delete its own folder instead of cleaning the whole root.

A cleanup failure is printed and the installer continues copying into that destination, which may leave a mixture of old and new content. Cleanup failure alone does not set a nonzero exit code. Inspect output as well as the exit status when automating cleanup. Copying has no rollback; see [Security and failures](docs/security-and-failures.md) for recovery.

## Draft Skills

Draft skills live in the repository beside the bundled ones, in `packages/skills/drafts/`, and are not published. The installer ignores them unless `--include-drafts` is given, which adds them to the skills it offers, each labeled `(draft)` in the wizard. The flag says where skills come from rather than what to install, so on its own it keeps the wizard; with other options, `--all-skills` and the default selection include the drafts too.

Run it from a checkout after building the package, from the directory to install into:

```sh
pnpm build skills
node "<checkout>/packages/skills/dist/cli.js" --include-drafts
```

Replace `<checkout>` with the path to the repository checkout. The build command runs from that checkout; run the `node` command from the project where the draft skills should be installed.

If no drafts exist, including in a published install, the flag fails with exit code `1`. A draft whose ID matches a bundled skill also fails. Use the published installer without this flag for normal installations.

## Automation Example

To extend our example to every supported workspace harness, replace the explicit harness list with `--all-harnesses`:

```sh
pnpm dlx @codenhub/skills@latest --local --all-harnesses --skills=brainstorming,test-driven-development
```

This creates every local destination in the table, even for tools you do not use. For a controlled setup script, the explicit Claude and Codex selection above is narrower. Pin an exact package version instead of `@latest` when the script must install the same released content on each run.

Next, read [Security and failures](docs/security-and-failures.md) to interpret exit codes and recover when only part of an install succeeds.

<!-- Source: docs/security-and-failures.md -->

# Install safely and recover from failures

Installing the [Claude and Codex example](docs/cli.md#repeat-the-selection-without-prompts) writes directly into two skills folders. This page explains what can change there, what the installer's path checks protect, and how to recover if copying fails. The installer reads and writes synchronously and has no rollback.

## Protect existing skills

By default, installation merges directories and overwrites files with matching paths. If you edited `.agents/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, installing that skill again replaces your edits. Back up customized skills before updating.

Files found only at the destination remain. An old reference file or a skill removed from a later package release stays installed until you remove it yourself. To remove one stale skill, delete that skill's directory in each destination where it was installed. The installer does not track which files it owns.

### Destructive cleanup

`--cleanup` recursively and forcibly removes every selected harness skills root before any skill is copied. For our local pair, that means all of `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`, including skills from other packages and manually managed files. Shared destinations are removed once, but every harness reading them is affected.

The roots are fixed by the selected harness and scope. Workspace roots resolve from the current working directory, and global roots from your home directory. Check both before running cleanup, and back up the entire selected roots. The [destination table](docs/cli.md#install-destinations) lists the paths.

Cleanup failures are printed as `Failed cleaning`, but installation continues into the affected destination. A cleanup failure alone does not set a nonzero exit code, so exit `0` does not prove that the directory was cleaned. In automation, inspect cleanup output as well as the exit status. If cleaning fails, resolve the reported filesystem problem and inspect the remaining content before trying again.

## Trust and path checks

Skills contain instructions an agent may follow and may carry scripts. Review their content and provenance before allowing an agent to use them. Choose trusted source trees when running from a checkout, grant only the filesystem permissions needed, and check that selected destinations are appropriate. The installer does not establish that the instructions or scripts are safe.

Before copying each skill, the installer resolves its source and as much of the destination path as already exists to their actual filesystem locations. It rejects a destination that resolves to the source itself or inside it, including through existing destination symlinks. This prevents recursive self-copying. If a checkout or symlink arrangement triggers this error, install into a separate directory outside that skill's source tree.

Source symlinks must resolve inside that individual skill's source tree. A link to a sibling skill or a file elsewhere is rejected with a directory traversal error. An accepted link is followed and its resolved contents are copied, rather than preserving the link. Canonical directories already visited are skipped to avoid symlink cycles. When authoring a skill, put needed files inside its own directory instead of linking to external files.

These checks constrain source reads and prevent self-copying; they are not a filesystem sandbox. They do not make an untrusted tree safe to copy into a sensitive destination. Filesystem state can also change between checks and operations. Avoid installing from attacker-controlled trees or into paths others can change during installation.

## Diagnose a failed install

The command prints failures and uses these exit codes:

- **`0`:** the selected copies succeeded, or help was printed. Selecting no skills or no harnesses in the wizard prints an exit message and also returns `0`, without installing. Cleanup failures can still have occurred.
- **`130`:** Ctrl+C cancelled the interactive wizard before installation. Run the installer again when ready to make a selection.
- **`1`:** invalid arguments, unknown skill IDs, harness labels invalid for the scope, no detected harness, missing skills, source-loading failures, an unhandled exception, or any skill copy failure. The error output identifies what to correct.

For argument errors, use the IDs in the [catalog](docs/skills.md#bundled-catalog) and scope-qualified labels in the [CLI guide](docs/cli.md#options). If no harness is detected, explicitly select the destinations you intend with `--harnesses`, or use `--all-harnesses` when you want every destination for the scope. Do not add cleanup to resolve a selection error.

If no skills are found or a bundled source cannot be read, use an intact package installation or restore the checkout's skill files. `--include-drafts` additionally fails when there are no drafts or a draft ID duplicates a bundled ID; omit the flag for published installations.

A copy can fail because its source disappeared, a path constraint was violated, or reading, resolving, creating, or writing a filesystem entry failed. The CLI reports `Failed copying` for each affected skill, then continues with remaining skills and destinations. It exits `1` after attempting them all. For permission errors, make the selected destination writable; for file/directory conflicts, back up and resolve the conflicting entry. Check the reported path before changing anything.

## Recover from partial writes

Copies are not transactional: files written before an error remain, overwritten files are not restored, and any successful cleanup is not undone. A later failure in Codex's destination does not undo a successful Claude installation. A failed skill copy may itself contain a mix of old and new files.

Inspect the reported skill and destination, fix the cause, and rerun the same selection without cleanup to copy missing or incomplete files again. Restore from your backup if you need the previous version or your local edits. A rerun still leaves destination-only files in place; inspect and remove stale files separately when necessary. Using `--cleanup` as recovery would also remove unrelated skills.

Next, review [Skill provenance](docs/provenance.md) for the origins and license notices that accompany the skills you install and share.

<!-- Source: docs/provenance.md -->

# Skill Provenance

When you install a skill in a project and share it with your team, its attribution needs to travel with it. This page records the origin and license context of the skills shipped by `@codenhub/skills`, so you can check what you are adopting before redistributing or modifying it.

The package-level legal terms are in [NOTICE](NOTICE). Each adapted skill also carries its attribution and upstream license text in its own directory, in `NOTICE` and, where the license is long, `LICENSE`, so both are copied when the installer copies that skill alone. For our `brainstorming` and `test-driven-development` example, their MIT notices accompany each copy installed for Claude and Codex.

| Skill                     | Origin                                 | License            |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `agents-md-improver`      | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `audit`                   | Adapted from [JuliusBrussee/caveman]   | MIT and Apache-2.0 |
| `babysit-pr`              | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `brainstorming`           | Adapted from [obra/superpowers]        | MIT                |
| `branding`                | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `caveman`                 | Adapted from [JuliusBrussee/caveman]   | MIT                |
| `caveman-commit`          | Adapted from [JuliusBrussee/caveman]   | MIT                |
| `coding`                  | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `design`                  | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `logo-design`             | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `motion-graphics`         | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `naming`                  | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `playful-tone`            | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `ponytail`                | Adapted from [DietrichGebert/ponytail] | MIT                |
| `ponytail-review`         | Adapted from [DietrichGebert/ponytail] | MIT                |
| `project-template`        | Original Coden Agency work             | Apache-2.0         |
| `subagent-specialist`     | Adapted from [obra/superpowers]        | MIT                |
| `test-driven-development` | Adapted from [obra/superpowers]        | MIT                |
| `writing-skills`          | Adapted from [obra/superpowers]        | MIT                |

The package `NOTICE` contains the applicable attribution blocks and bundled MIT license text. Preserve the relevant notices and license text when sharing installed directories, and review the license terms before modifying or redistributing them.

Return to [Bundled skills](docs/skills.md) to choose another workflow, or the [CLI installer](docs/cli.md) to install it. Before updating an existing installation, review the [changelog](docs/changelog/index.md) and [overwrite and recovery behavior](docs/security-and-failures.md).

[dietrichgebert/ponytail]: https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail
[juliusbrussee/caveman]: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman
[obra/superpowers]: https://github.com/obra/superpowers

<!-- Source: docs/changelog/0.3.0.md -->

# 0.3.0

## Added

- Documentation in Brazilian Portuguese and Spanish: the README and every public page except the changelog.
- `babysit-pr` answers requests made in review summaries and conversation comments with one pull request comment per round.
- `test-driven-development` covers refactors meant to keep behavior: confirm tests cover it, adding passing characterization tests where they do not, then refactor.

## Changed

- **Breaking.** The package exports no JavaScript API. `parseFrontmatter`, `getSkills`, and `copyRecursiveSync` are gone from the public surface, and `main`, `module`, and `types` with them; only `@codenhub/skills/package.json` resolves. They could not reach the bundled skills, so the installer is the supported way to get them. Copy a skill directory from the package's `skills/` folder if you need it outside the installer.
- The docs are rewritten around choosing skills and installing them, with a catalog that says when an agent uses each skill.
- `babysit-pr` starts when asked to monitor a pull request or handle its CI and reviews, or after opening one as part of a task the user asked to see through, not after every push. Its report lists only failing, rerun, or unfixable checks, names each declined comment once, and holds decision questions for the report unless they block all progress. A bot nitpick fixed as suggested gets a one-line reply.
- `brainstorming` no longer gates bug fixes whose expected behavior is already clear, and its final step summarizes only what changed since the sections were approved.
- `caveman` turns off whenever the user asks for normal style, writes code, comments, commits, pull requests, and files in normal style, keeps real uncertainty, and uses the lite level when the user only asks for shorter answers.
- `caveman-commit` commits, stages, or amends when the user asks for that, follows the project's commit convention when `git log` shows one other than Conventional Commits, and keeps co-author trailers the workflow requires.
- `ponytail` builds everything a complex request asks for, the simplest way, and questions only the extras it skipped.
- `test-driven-development` ships a fix without a test only with the user's approval, and says so in the report. It captures a verification baseline before coding.
- `design` no longer loads for motion graphics. `logo-design` loads for app icons and favicons, not interface icons. `audit` leaves over-engineering reviews out of scope. `project-template` audits only template-based projects.
- `motion-graphics` sets minimum text sizes against the frame's shorter side, with larger minimums for vertical video on phones, holds the end only on a call to action or logo, and always seeds randomness.
- `project-template` reads the template as an `owner/repo` and fetches its default branch instead of `main`, and states that it needs `git`, `pnpm`, and an authenticated `gh`.

## Fixed

- `branding` applied 3:1 contrast to small labels and button text; text below 24px, or 18.66px bold, now needs 4.5:1.
- `project-template`'s local start removed the clone's history before recording the template commit, and its placeholder check missed placeholders outside a fixed list.
- `babysit-pr` could never finish on a pull request whose AI reviewer comments after every push.
- `branding` and `logo-design` told agents to resolve the font and output paths inside the installed skill folder.
- Contradictions between examples and rules, and between `SKILL.md` files and their references or Codex metadata, in `audit`, `ponytail`, `ponytail-review`, `test-driven-development`, `subagent-specialist`, `agents-md-improver`, `writing-skills`, `brainstorming`, `branding`, `motion-graphics`, `naming`, `playful-tone`, `caveman`, and `caveman-commit`.

<!-- Source: docs/changelog/0.2.0.md -->

# 0.2.0

## Added

- `audit`, which audits and reviews code, pull requests, and packages and classifies every finding the same way. It replaces `caveman-review`.
- `design`, which guides visual and interface design in any medium: hierarchy, typography, space, color, interaction, and interface motion. It replaces `frontend-design`.
- `naming`, which generates, researches, and judges names for products, packages, tools, and code identifiers, and verifies each presented name's meaning, pronunciation, and collisions.
- `branding`, which builds brand strategy and identity systems, from positioning and voice to visual identity, guidelines, and presentations.
- `logo-design`, which designs logos from written concepts to outlined SVG files and usage rules, with a script that outlines lettering with the font's kerning.
- `motion-graphics`, which storyboards, animates, and renders videos frame by frame from a seekable timeline, with any encoder the environment has.
- `ponytail` and `ponytail-review`, which keep code to the simplest solution that works and review a diff for over-engineering.
- `babysit-pr`, which sees a pull request through CI and review until it is ready to merge, fixing failing checks and answering reviewers.
- `project-template`, which creates, syncs, and adopts projects built on the shared project template.
- `playful-tone`, which gives docs and public text a natural, playful tone in any language.
- **Stable.** The package is no longer experimental.
- The installer covers Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Windsurf, Trae, Cline, Kiro, ZCode, and the cross-harness Agent Skills location (`.agents/skills`). Harnesses that read the same directory get one copy of each skill.
- A CLI guide, a skill format and catalog page, and a provenance page.

## Changed

- **Breaking.** Node.js 24 or newer is required, up from 18.
- **Breaking.** Codex skills install to `.agents/skills` in the workspace and `~/.agents/skills` globally, where Codex now reads them, instead of `.codex/skills` and `~/.codex/skills`. Skills installed by 0.1.0 stay in the old directory until you delete them.
- `writing-skills`, `agents-md-improver`, `subagent-specialist`, `test-driven-development`, `brainstorming`, `caveman`, and `caveman-commit` are rewritten or revised. `writing-skills` is organized around the Agent Skills specification's rules and an evaluation procedure.
- Bundled skills no longer name other skills, since the user may not have them installed.

## Removed

- **Breaking.** `frontend-design`, replaced by `design`, and `caveman-review`, folded into `audit`. The installer does not remove a skill's old directory, so delete `frontend-design` and `caveman-review` from each skills destination by hand.
